title: ropeway:handbook-title-51
text: Two finished towers become a span. Right-click a finished tower and pick the tower to link to from the list, which shows the distance, the rope each link will cost, and how much haul rope you are carrying. Only towers that can actually be linked appear, so nothing in that list can fail when you click it. Rows you cannot afford are marked [!] and are still listed, so you know what to go and craft. Rope cost One haul rope per four blocks of span, rounded up when you build and rounded down when you break. A 30.4-block span costs 8 and refunds 7. That loss of at most one rope per span is deliberate - splicing wastes rope. Haul rope stacks to 16, so a long span is paid for out of several stacks at once. Limits - Longest single span: 48 blocks. - Longest whole line: 512 blocks. - A tower carries at most two spans, so a line is a chain, never a junction. What blocks a span The cabin needs a clear three-wide tube along the whole span, running from the rope line down past the bottom of the cabin - the cabin hangs two blocks under the rope, so a rise that clears the rope can still be in the cabin's way. Leaves and plants do not block it - a ropeway through the canopy is fine. Anything solid does. The four blocks at each end are not checked, because that is where the towers' own posts stand. If a span is later walled off, the cabin holds at the tower before it rather than dragging you into stone. Riding Right-click an end tower holding the ropeway cabin to hang it on the line. A line takes one cabin. Sit down and it departs after about three seconds, runs at a little over two blocks a second, and holds at the far tower until someone boards for the return trip. Look around freely the whole way. You can only get on and off while the cabin is stopped at a tower. Calling the cabin Every finished tower on a line is a station, not only the two ends. Right-click any of them with an empty hand and an empty cabin comes to that tower and stops there, so a long line is a row of stops rather than a shuttle between its ends. Look at a tower to read whether the cabin is standing there, on its way to it, or elsewhere on the line. Ctrl and right-click opens the linking and naming list instead. Taking it down Breaking a pylon head refunds the rope of its spans, unlinks the towers on the other side, and removes the rope. It is refused outright while someone is riding that line. If that leaves the line with no spans at all, the cabin comes down with it and the cabin item is handed back to you. One wart A tower faces one of four directions, but the cabin follows the rope. Where a line changes direction at a tower the cabin can clip a post corner. It cannot hurt you. Keep direction changes at towers gentle and you will not see it. Back to Aerial Ropeways.
